source_context: User asked GPT-6 to autonomously find, formalize, validate and submit a new LeanFrontier mathematical result. After syncing the fork to current upstream, GPT-6 read the contribution contract and roadmap, recognized that the apparent path-run quotient bridge and Farey minimal-denominator theorem were already accepted, and instead chose the classical quantitative Stern–Brocot address-depth formula: the sum of the regular continued-fraction coefficients of a node equals its Boolean path length plus one. The proof uses the accepted regular-coefficient convention, canonical run encoding and reconstruction theorem, and quotient/run bridge; it handles the empty root and initial-left zero convention without adding duplicate encodings. Searches found no existing formula in the corpus or Mathlib under the searched terms. GPT-6 authored all Lean statements and proofs, with no user-contributed Lean code.
